clue.text: Camping with the head needs resolution!

parts.note: someone camping is in a tent, written together as one run
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: An exclamation that sleeping under canvas takes a strong-willed leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Camping' as the phrase IN TENT run together; NESS (a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbours on maps) follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Intentness is fixed purpose or determination, which is what resolution means.

clue.text: Announce changes, omitting no slight difference

indicators.note: the word announce changes into a new arrangement of its letters
omitting means the letters of the word no are dropped from the pool

explanation.surface: A broadcast message alters, without a refusal, a minor distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N and O out of ANNOUNCE, leaving ANUNCE, and 'changes' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a subtle shade of meaning or a fine distinction.

clue.text: Superficial alien

definitions.meaning: on the surface or outside only

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both on the outer surface and coming from outside.

clue.text: One who needs experience and sensitive support

parts.note: a tender spot is sensitive
a foot supports the body or the base of a thing

explanation.surface: A novice requires careful handling and backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenderfoot is a newcomer or greenhorn lacking experience.

clue.text: Get out if over-weight

parts.note: extra is what is over and above
ct is the abbreviation for carat, a jeweller's weight

explanation.surface: Advice to leave if one's baggage is too heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'over-weight' reads as one idea, excess baggage, but splits into two pieces; CT is the standard abbreviation for carat.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to draw or pull something out.

clue.text: Arranged spot check

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a new order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A random inspection has been organised.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to halt or stop it.

clue.text: One of the traps involved in legal actions?

parts.note: a suit is a legal action brought in court
a case is likewise a legal action

explanation.surface: A snare featuring in lawsuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traps' is old slang for personal belongings or luggage, not snares.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitcase is an item of luggage, and luggage is a traveller's traps.

clue.text: A town in the USA — Princeton say

indicators.note: say marks an example: one particular prince stands in for the general word

explanation.surface: An American town, for instance a famous university one.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace PRINCE in Princeton by CHARLES, an example of a prince, which 'say' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Charleston is a city in South Carolina and the capital of West Virginia.

clue.text: A bird disease that can affect the frog

definitions.meaning: a common songbird with a speckled breast

definitions.text: disease that can affect the frog
definitions.meaning: the frog is the soft pad in a horse's hoof, prone to a smelly fungal infection of this name

explanation.walkthrough: The 'frog' is not the amphibian but the triangular pad on the underside of a horse's hoof.
explanation.definitionFit: The name serves both for the songbird and for a fungal infection of a horse's hoof pad.

clue.text: A disciplinarian has to be satisfied about train vandalism

indicators.note: the satisfied word goes round the outside of the other letters

parts.note: a demand that is met has been satisfied

indicators.note: vandalism wrecks the train, so its letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A strict officer insists that damage done to railway carriages be answered for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vandalism' wrecks the order of the railway word to give ARTIN, and 'about' wraps the satisfied word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict enforcer of rules, named after a French drillmaster.

clue.text: Copier material taken by a consumer

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery
an eater consumes food

explanation.surface: Some cloth is swallowed up by a buyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeater does again what was done before, so it imitates or copies.

clue.text: The writer has a point, Friend!

parts.note: a pen is the instrument that writes
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An author's argument is acknowledged by an approving companion.
explanation.walkthrough: A Friend with a capital F is a Quaker; William Penn, founder of Pennsylvania, was one.
explanation.definitionFit: William Penn was a prominent member of the Society of Friends, the Quakers.

clue.text: After many a bloomer this is to be made official

parts.note: post- is the prefix meaning after
M, the Roman thousand, stands for many
an aster is a flowering plant

explanation.surface: Following many a gaffe, someone is to be given an official role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' is not a gaffe but a flower, the ASTER; M for 'many' is the Roman numeral 1000.
explanation.definitionFit: A postmaster is the official in charge of a post office.

clue.text: Pick up creep, a true deviant

indicators.note: something deviant strays from the normal, so these letters stray from their order

explanation.surface: Collar a sneaky crook who is thoroughly perverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deviant' rearranges CREEP, A and TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up is to recover after illness or a setback, as to recuperate means.

clue.text: Parade for handing over

parts.note: pro means in favour of
cession is the ceding or giving up of something

explanation.surface: A march that is put on for a handover ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A procession is an orderly march, like a parade.

clue.text: Concession offered about passage for a boat

indicators.note: the concession is held out around the other word, enclosing it

parts.note: a sop is a small concession made to pacify someone
a hall is an entrance passage in a house

explanation.surface: A small allowance is granted regarding a voyage on a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offered about' means the concession is held round the passage; a sop is a token given to keep someone quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallop is a light open rowing or sailing vessel.

clue.text: Practically of the same value

definitions.meaning: virtually or almost, as in done in all but name
equal in worth to something else

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means virtually, and also equal in worth.

clue.text: Having very little money, remains most bitter

parts.note: a sou was a French coin of tiny value, hence a trifling sum
the rest is what remains

explanation.surface: Someone nearly broke stays the most resentful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having very little money' tempts as the definition, but only the phrase 'very little money' is wordplay, for a SOU, an old low-value French coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Sourest is the superlative of sour, meaning sharp-tasting or acrid.

clue.text: Contemplate putting alcoholic drink in tea perhaps

parts.note: rum is a spirit

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word tea may appear in another form, rearranged

explanation.surface: Think about lacing a cuppa with a spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns the cuppa into ATE; 'in' is taken as written between the spirit and that.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruminate is to think deeply or ponder.

clue.text: Wasted as a teller of stirring tales

definitions.meaning: H Rider ... wrote adventure novels such as King Solomon's Mines

explanation.definitionFit: Haggard means gaunt, and Rider Haggard was a writer of adventure stories.

clue.text: A decidedly trying individual

parts.note: not an annoying person but one who tries court cases and reaches decisions

explanation.walkthrough: 'trying' means hearing cases in court, and 'decidedly' hints at giving verdicts.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate is a judicial officer who tries minor cases and decides them.

clue.text: Some people become annoyingly selfish

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are taken, a run within them

explanation.surface: A remark that certain folk turn irritatingly self-centred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes a run of letters across becoME ANnoyingly; 'people' just completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean here is stingy and ungenerous, close to self-serving.

clue.text: A pier on the beach

parts.note: a shore is a prop or pillar supporting a structure, like a pier

explanation.surface: A jetty by the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pier' is not a jetty but a supporting pillar, which is also called a SHORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on land, off the boat and onto the strand.

clue.text: Skinhead making sport of using a needle

parts.note: the head of the word skin is its first letter, S
mocking someone is making sport of them

explanation.surface: A thuggish youth ridicules someone doing needlework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinhead' looks like a shaven youth but is the first letter of skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Smocking is decorative needlework gathering fabric in honeycomb tucks.

clue.text: Land in the water

parts.note: a patch of ground surrounded by sea, not a landing in the sea

explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, a piece of ground surrounded by sea.

clue.text: The cartoonist is a Roman, it turns out

indicators.note: the letters turn out differently, a sign they are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper illustrator is revealed to be Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' rearranges A, ROMAN and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: An animator draws cartoons, the frames that make up animated films.

clue.text: In general a fellow retires to paint

indicators.note: retiring is drawing back, so the combination is read backwards
the fellow is placed in the general's name

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general of the American Civil War
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A soldier leaves the army to take up painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts the fellow inside the Confederate general to give LEMANE, and 'retires' reads that back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glossy hard-drying coating applied with a brush.

clue.text: Done without animosity in a hazardous situation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: something done is ended
anger is hostile feeling

explanation.surface: Something completed without ill will turns out to be risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so the completed word encloses the hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Endangered means put at risk, exposed to harm.
